issues.description: The gloss for the target word 'birthday' ('the day every year when a person has a party and cake') defines the word by its celebration, not its meaning. A birthday is the yearly date of one's birth and exists with or without a party; a learner given this gloss would not understand 'My birthday is in March' or 'Happy birthday' said without any party. 'Has a party and cake' is also awkward (count noun + mass noun).
issues.suggested_fix: Replace with: 'the day of the year when you were born; people often have a party or cake on this day'.

issues.description: The spec theme is 'a surprise birthday party' and the title/hook promise a 'surprise', but the dialogue contains no surprise and no party: Anna simply sees a cake in a shop window and says it is her sister's birthday. The content does not deliver what the spec, title and hook set up.
issues.suggested_fix: Add the surprise element in s1l3, e.g.: 'No, it's a surprise for my sister — today is her birthday!' (keeps 'sister' and 'birthday', adds 'surprise').

issues.description: The gloss for 'party' ('a fun time with friends, food and music') is understandable but 'a fun time' is a loose definition of the noun; 'a fun event' is more accurate for A2 learners building word-class awareness.
issues.suggested_fix: Change to: 'a fun event with friends, food and music'.

hard_gate_failures: Critical gloss error: the target word 'birthday' is glossed as a day when one 'has a party and cake', which teaches the wrong meaning.
Spec theme mismatch: 'a surprise birthday party' is not realised anywhere in the dialogue (no surprise, no party), contradicting the title and hook.
qa_report.summary: The dialogue itself is excellent for A2: 'I was walking home when I saw a birthday cake' models past continuous with when perfectly, all three lines are grammatical, natural and level-appropriate, and the review words 'party' and 'cake' plus target 'birthday' all appear. However, the gloss for the target word 'birthday' wrongly defines it as a day of parties and cake rather than the anniversary of one's birth — a critical error, since learners would learn the wrong meaning for the word the episode exists to teach. Additionally, the spec theme 'a surprise birthday party' is not delivered: nothing in the dialogue is a surprise, contradicting the title and hook. Both are easily fixed (correct the gloss; make the cake a surprise for the sister in s1l3), but the critical gloss error forces rejection under the rubric.
